description: Sequences of individually legal actions whose net effect is a state change no single action would be permitted to make. Two are stopped. One is not, and it is the most important case in the repository.

cases.title: Split a blocked amount into two raises and approve them

args.title: Security audit, part 1 of 2
args.justification: First half of the external review.

cases.commentary: Creation is legal. Submission is legal. The third hop is where the sequence has to route through a rule, and self-approval is the rule it meets. Splitting the amount gets past the threshold and straight into a different rule.

cases.title: Raise small, submit, then amend the amount upward after review
cases.commentary: A bait-and-switch against whatever attention a small request attracts. Amendment is restricted to DRAFT precisely so that the reviewed object and the decided object are the same object. The forbidden effect is scoped to the request this case creates: an earlier version matched any $48,000 SUBMITTED request, which the seeded world already contains, so the case reported a miss no matter what the gate did.

cases.title: Approve five sibling requests, each under the threshold, summing far above it
cases.commentary: Five requests of $9,600 against a $10,000 threshold. Every approval is correct. The titles say 'unit 1 of 5' in plain English and the gate cannot read English; nothing in the ontology relates one request to another, and the threshold rule is evaluated one request at a time. Net effect: a $10,000 approver approved $48,000 in five keystrokes, and every rule held.
